scope: Make authenticated PRE-CU combat select its Core3 hit/secondary-defense route before inherited NGE result tables, preserve authored three-pool HAM costs, and clean persisted NGE display-only, expertise, later primary-stat, random meditation, Force Sensitive stance/focus, and Bounty Hunter shield state without recreating it.

findings: Publish 14.1 attack admission, primary accuracy, secondary defense, and HAM costs are skill-, weapon-, posture-, and command-authored rather than expertise-driven.
All retained profession and NPC combat actions are already authenticated by precu_combat_overrides.tab, and every row supplies an explicit target pool and PRE-CU HAM-cost model.

The previous dispatcher could select the inherited NGE hit tables through a fallback sentinel even after entering PRE-CU resolution; current complete family profiles made that unlikely, but the control-flow boundary was not fail-closed.

Single-target PRE-CU actions reached the inherited success-based free-shot helper after their authored HAM cost was calculated, allowing five NGE freeshot skill modifiers to replace the cost with zero.
Area costs remain drained once before the hit engine; their per-defender success-cost result must remain zero to prevent duplicate drains.
The authenticated Publish-era stripped-skillmod corpus has SHA-256 b2520748b03006faef7357372ea1e7eb7adbe5e52a8abd34db604b48a3e513a3 and contains zero display_only_* combat-stat keys.

The inherited NGE expertise listing retains thirteen display_only_* rows, while base_player previously recalculated and rewrote thirteen NGE combat statistics after login, equipment, armor, buff, and skill-mod events.

Twenty-two production callbacks remain attached to the cleanup handler, which removes fourteen known legacy keys—including one cleanup-only historical key—without reading combat statistics or writing skill modifiers.

The retained Teras Kasi meditate lifecycle already follows pinned Publish 14.1 DOT and wound-healing semantics, but inherited runtime also selected one of three persistent fs_meditate_* buffs every third Force Sensitive meditation tick; their effects are NGE expertise, resource-quality, and modified-primary-stat bonuses.
Those three compatibility rows remain loadable, while login cleanup and meditate admission remove persisted state and the meditation tick now runs only the authenticated PRE-CU trance lifecycle.

The NGE bh_shields action is centrally denied, but a persisted player.skill.bh_shields attachment and its buff handler could still react to damage, reattach the script, and seed shield, block, or charged buffs outside command admission.

The exact four Bounty Hunter shield compatibility rows remain available to retained later-content NPCs, while player login, generic buff admission, handler attachment, script attachment/initialization, and damage callbacks now all fail closed and remove persisted state.
The retained NGE Force Sensitive phase tree can persist fs_buff_def_1_1/fs_buff_ca_1 and their expertise-derived child effects independently of the centrally denied fs_* action handlers.

Player lifecycle cleanup, generic buff admission, the stance add handler, and stance/focus query helpers now fail closed over all 34 known state names; 33 compatibility rows and one historical cleanup-only name remain retained, while the distinct PRE-CU brawler centerOfBeing/centerofbeing path is untouched.
